meta.title: How Time Flies By
meta.footerNote: Beat outline · bullets to hit, not final VO

sections.label: Cold Open
sections.sublabel: Drop into the moment the tweet finally landed
sections.purpose: Stop the scroll and plant a question. One job: make a stranger need to know what happened to you. You're not introducing yourself or the topic — you read one provocative line and admit something in you changed. If the viewer doesn't feel a question forming by 0:15, nothing else in the video gets watched.

items.text: Talk about the tweet — open cold, no intro, no "hey guys," read it out loud word for word: "Once you realize just how much more work it takes to go from good to great…you realize you can only be great at a few things and ignore the rest."
Talk about how you'd read this tweet many times and it never did anything — until this read, when it hit. Don't explain why yet. [PLACEHOLDER — roughly how many times you'd read it]
Pivot line: "I'd read this tweet a dozen times. This was the first time it meant something."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Quiet, suspended. Don't compete with the tweet read. Single sustained note under the pivot line.

shotList.desc: Open mid-scroll on phone or laptop. The actual tweet on the actual scroll. No intro, no logo, no "hey everyone."
Full-screen tweet text overlay during the verbatim read.
Cut to face on the pivot line. Quiet, not performed.

sections.label: Promise
sections.sublabel: Name the viewer and the deal
sections.purpose: Tell the viewer who this is for and what they get — in one sentence — so they choose to stay on purpose, not by accident. You're not previewing the content; you're making a single promise big enough to be worth nine minutes. Goal: they think "that's me, and I need to see this."

items.text: Talk about who this video is for — pick one: (a) the employed-and-comfortable past version of you, (b) anyone in their 20s who thinks they have time. [DECIDE]
Talk about the deal — by the end, the viewer should see why the years they think they have are already half-spent.

Talk about the one promise — don't list takeaways, just one sentence: "By the end I'm going to show you the math that gutted me — and why if you're employed right now, you're sitting on the only window you'll ever have."

musicCue.title: (carries over from Cold Open)
musicCue.desc: No transition. Light build cued for pivot into The Break.

shotList.desc: Direct camera, slightly tighter framing. No B-roll yet — viewer should be locked on the face.

sections.label: The Break
sections.sublabel: The belief that cracked: "I had time."
sections.purpose: Name the belief that ran your life for five years: "I'm good, good is enough, and I have time." This is the lie the entire video exists to take apart. You're showing how reasonable it felt at the time, so the viewer recognizes it in their own life instead of dismissing you as careless.

items.text: Talk about the belief that cracked — confess it out loud, full sentence: "For five years I thought I was good, and I thought that was enough."

Talk about why it made sense — walk through the evidence you had at the time: two jobs, two incomes, living abroad, taxes optimized, savings climbing. Say the numbers if you're willing. [PLACEHOLDER — pick which numbers go on camera]

Talk about the warning sign you kept ignoring — was there ONE moment (a friend's comment, a recruiter message, an itch on a Sunday) where you knew the second skill was missing? [PLACEHOLDER — find the moment]
Don't resolve it yet. End on: "I didn't feel lazy. I felt earned. That was the trap."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Push forward subtly. Tension building, not yet released.

shotList.desc: Direct address. This is the confession — eyes locked, no cuts away during the belief statement.
Optional: pull-quote overlay on the closing line.

sections.label: Scene 1
sections.sublabel: The Peak — when you thought you'd made it
sections.purpose: Show the good life at its best so the fall has height to fall from. Make the comfort look genuinely earned and enviable — money, freedom, the dream actually hit — while planting one small unease. Don't moralize yet; let the viewer enjoy it with you so it costs them something when it goes.

items.text: Talk about the specific month and place where the peak was. [PLACEHOLDER — what city, what month, what year]
Talk about a sensory detail of comfort — morning routine, evening rhythm, the texture of your weekday. What did "comfortable" actually feel like in your body?
Talk about the high school dream out loud — money on the internet, travel, retire early. Then say: "And I had done all three."
Talk about the numbers, if you'll say them — two incomes for one person's hours, tax savings, monthly burn. [PLACEHOLDER — decide what's on camera]
Talk about one foreshadowing beat — was there a moment in the peak where something didn't sit right? Even small. A Sunday feeling. A quiet question. [PLACEHOLDER]

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Warm, slightly nostalgic. The good times — but a small unease underneath.

shotList.desc: [TBD] — old footage / photos from the abroad period if you have any. If not, recreate the routine.
Mix with B-roll. Voice over the visual.
Numbers on screen if you'll show them: salary, savings rate, hours/week.

sections.label: Scene 2
sections.purpose: Both incomes vanish — this is the inciting event, where the story actually starts. Stay inside the scene, don't narrate from today: where you were, what you felt, the first morning with nothing. End it hollow, not sad; the viewer should feel the floor drop.

items.text: Talk about the first firing — the moment itself. Where were you? What time of day? Who told you? What did you do in the next hour? [PLACEHOLDER]
Talk about what happened, what you felt, what you did — don't editorialize from the present, be there.
Talk about the second firing — how long after the first? Did you see it coming or did it ambush you? [PLACEHOLDER]
Talk about the first morning waking up with no jobs at all — what was the first thought? One real sentence.
Land the scene on: "For the first time in five years, nobody needed me at a computer."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Drop. Something sparse, hollow. Don't make it sad — make it quiet.

shotList.desc: Close framing for the firings. Let the viewer sit with you.
[TBD] — desk, empty calendar, the apartment in the morning.

sections.label: Scene 3
sections.sublabel: Starting Over — the math is brutal
sections.purpose: Show that the way out is brutal once you do the math. Be honest about how long you thought it would take versus reality, and let the fear questions hang without answers. The point: there is no easy escape — that's exactly what makes the tweet's lesson land later.

items.text: Talk about when the YouTube decision happened — was it a clear moment or a slow drift? [PLACEHOLDER — find the day or the week]
Talk about what you thought it would take — three months? Six? A year? Say the wrong number out loud; viewers connect to it more than the right one.
Talk about the first reality check — what was the first thing that took 10x longer than expected? Editing? Writing? Thumbnails? The first script? [PLACEHOLDER — pick the one that hit you hardest]

Talk about the fear questions but DON'T resolve them — will the savings last? Will you have to go back to the US? Manual labor? Will anyone even hire you with AI eating the market? Say them out loud once, then move on.

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Working music — but anxious, not hopeful.

shotList.desc: [TBD] — your actual editing timeline, Notion, blank doc, whatever the start-over looked like.
Direct on the fear questions. One sentence each, no list framing.

sections.label: Scene 4
sections.sublabel: The Tweet Lands — return to the cold open
sections.purpose: Return to the cold open now that the viewer has the full story, and pay off the open loop you planted at 0:15. Walk the actual math out loud so the realization happens with them, not at them. This is the emotional turn: the regret was never getting fired — it's the five years before it.

items.text: Talk about the cold open moment again — now the viewer has the context. Walk through what shifted in your head between then and now.

Talk about the tweet again — read it, then walk through the math out loud: ten years to good at code, five years coasted, how many years to good at THIS new thing? [PLACEHOLDER — say the honest number]
Talk about what you did for the rest of that day after it hit — did you tell anyone? Did you write anything down? Did you keep scrolling? [PLACEHOLDER — the unglamorous answer is the better one]
Land the scene on: "I wasn't sad I got fired. I was sad about the five years before that."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Mirror the Cold Open music. Same texture, now with weight under it.

shotList.desc: Return to the same chair, same scroll. Visual symmetry with Cold Open.
Re-show the tweet with on-screen math: years to good, years to great, years coasted.
Locked face on the closing line. No cuts.

sections.label: Scene 5
sections.sublabel: The Animation Math — three hours, four seconds
sections.purpose: Make the lesson physical and present-tense: three hours of work, four seconds of finished video. Project the math forward on camera and ask the question without answering it. This is the lowest point of the video — do not rescue it; the discomfort is the payload.

items.text: Talk about the ratio — three hours of work, four seconds of output. Say it out loud.
Talk about the math projected forward on camera — at this rate, X hours = Y minutes of finished video = Z videos a year. Run the actual numbers, don't sanitize. [PLACEHOLDER]
Talk about the question — ask it and don't answer it: "Does the math close before the savings run out?"
Talk about letting the silence sit — this is the lowest point of the video, don't rescue it.

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Sparse to silent. Let the math do the work. Drop the music entirely on the unanswered question.

shotList.desc: Open on the actual animation editor — Premiere / After Effects / whatever. Real timeline, real timestamp visible.
On-screen math: hours / output / projected runway. Numbers do the talking.
Cut to face on the unanswered question. Hold. Don't blink past it.

sections.label: The Lesson
sections.sublabel: Close the loop, crystallize, leave them with one move
sections.purpose: Close every loop and hand the viewer one move they can make tonight. Crystallize the whole video into one screenshot-able line, generalize it to them in a sentence, then give a single concrete action — not a list. The job isn't to inspire; it's to make them feel the price of their own comfortable years before the video ends.

items.text: Talk about closing the loop — bring the viewer back to the cold open moment one final time.
I didn't lose my job. I lost five years I could've spent becoming great at something else — and I gave them away to be comfortable.
Talk about the generalization for the viewer in ONE sentence: comfort is the most expensive thing you'll ever buy with your time, and you only notice the bill when the comfort is gone.

Talk about ONE specific action you're handing the viewer — something they can do tonight. Suggested: "If you're employed and comfortable right now, pick one skill you'd want to be great at in five years and put one hour into it before you go to bed."

musicCue.title: [TBD]
musicCue.desc: Bring the Cold Open music back, fuller now. Resolution, not relief.
musicCue.note: Cut music two beats before the action prompt. Last line should be dry.

shotList.desc: Visual return to Cold Open — same chair, same scroll. Symmetry closes the story.
Locked face for the crystallized line. No cuts. No movement.
Pull-quote overlay on the crystallized line — large, screenshotable.
Action prompt direct to camera. Slight forward lean if you want.
NO like/sub before the lesson lands. Like/sub end-card goes AFTER the action prompt.
